key_insight: Explicitly enforcing person–garment correspondence inside Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) causes correspondence to emerge reliably and preserves fine garment details in unpaired virtual try-on. CORAL analyzes 3D attention and injects alignment constraints so DiT-based VTONs better map garment pixels to the correct body regions.
problem_solved: Virtual try-on systems (especially DiT-based) struggle to preserve fine garment detail and lack explicit mechanisms or explanations for person–garment correspondence in unpaired settings, producing misaligned or blurred clothing outputs.
method: Analyze full 3D attention patterns in Diffusion Transformer architectures to identify how and when person–garment correspondence forms or degrades.

Introduce CORAL — a correspondence alignment module/constraint that enforces precise person–garment alignment within the attention mechanism (via attention regularization and correspondence supervision), so mappings emerge robustly without paired training data.
Train the model with combined generative diffusion objectives plus correspondence-alignment signals to preserve fine details and improve realism in the synthesized try-on images.
impact: Enables more realistic, detail-preserving virtual try-on results and makes DiT attention more interpretable and controllable. Useful for practitioners building conditioned image synthesis, fashion applications, and any pipeline that needs robust spatial correspondence from generative transformers.
visual_elements: Before/after try-on image pairs highlighting improved preservation of fine garment details (e.g., logos, seams, textures).
Heatmap visualizations of DiT 3D attention with and without CORAL to show improved person–garment correspondence.
Architecture diagram showing where CORAL integrates into the DiT pipeline (input, attention module, alignment supervision).
Bar/line chart comparing quantitative metrics (detail-preservation, perceptual quality, alignment scores) for baseline vs CORAL-enhanced models.
paper_title: CORAL: Correspondence Alignment for Improved Virtual Try-On
paper_authors: Jiyoung Kim, Youngjin Shin, Siyoon Jin, Dahyun Chung, Jisu Nam
